claim: Restores of S3 objects are skipped if the destination bucket has an object with the same name or version ID. When you restore to the original S3 bucket, AWS Backup does not perform a destructive restore: it will not put an object into the bucket in place of an object that already exists, regardless of version; but a delete marker in the current version is treated as the object being nonexistent, so a restore can occur.

qualifiers.condition: a current-version delete marker counts as no object, so that object can be restored

evidence.quote: Restores of objects are skipped if the destination bucket has an object with the same name or version ID.

When you restore to the original S3 bucket, AWS Backup does not perform a destructive restore, which means AWS Backup will not put an object into a bucket in place of an object that already exists, regardless of version.
A delete marker in the current version is treated as the object as nonexistent, so a restore can occur.
